summary: Luke Badiali ran the first session with Paul Ingram and Rebecca Shaw on who Thornbury should target. The firm sells to too many sectors with a mix of gain-share and fixed fees. We agreed to focus on PE portfolio companies with £50m to £300m revenue and third-party spend above £20m.

discussion.keyPoints: Rebecca said 22 consultants are spread across 14 sectors. Paul noted PE portfolio companies made up 35% of fees but most of the repeat work.
Gain-share deals have strong margins but long payment tails; fixed-fee work is predictable but often discounted. Paul is attached to gain-share as the firm's signature.
Main competitors are two national procurement consultancies and freelance interim category managers. Thornbury wins on speed of savings identification.

recommendations.recommendation: Target PE portfolio companies with £50m to £300m revenue and third-party spend over £20m, with the CFO as the buyer.
Position Thornbury as the firm that finds bankable savings in 12 weeks, ahead of the next lender covenant test.
Drop low-margin public sector bids and narrow to 4 sectors: food manufacturing, logistics, business services and healthcare services.
Win 8 new PE portfolio clients in the next 12 months through PE operating partners rather than direct to CFOs.

actions.action: Pull fees and margin by sector for the last three years

nextFocus: Build the value proposition and narrative for PE-backed CFOs.
nextPreparation: Paul to bring three savings case examples with verified figures.

tests.question: Who did we agree is our ideal customer?
Is narrowing to four sectors agreed?
